# Threagile threat-model analysis mis-rates findings and mangles their wording, without a test suite

A tool that reads a written description of a system, judges where that design is dangerous, and writes up what it saw now gets both the judgement and the wording wrong in many places. No description was changed and the document format did not change, yet the same models come back graded differently than before, some write-ups read as garbled, and in a few places something is reported where nothing should be reported at all while elsewhere a danger quietly stops being reported. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

Writing the description down. Splitting a model across a lead document plus further documents no longer yields the same content as keeping the very same model in a single document: the free prose describing the system as a whole ends up carrying only the words contributed by the second document, rather than both joined together, so the two ways of writing one model no longer agree. The words that name levels are read back wrongly in four ways. A blank seriousness word, which stands for the medium level, resolves one step away from medium, although every spelled-out level still reads right. A blank word for how probable exploitation is, which stands for likely, likewise resolves to the wrong level while the named ones are fine.
